units.speaker: Vasiṣṭha
units.devanagari:
निर्मिता मायया भीमाः पक्षक्षुब्धा इवाद्रयः |
उदगुस्ते महामाया दामो व्यालः कटस्तथा ||
units.iast:
nirmitā māyayā bhīmāḥ pakṣakṣubdhā ivādrayaḥ |
udaguste mahāmāyā dāmo vyālaḥ kaṭastathā ||
units.english: {0:Fashioned} {1:by māyā}, {2:terrible}, {4:like} {5:mountains} {3:with their wings heaving}, {7:those} {8:possessors of great māyā} {6:arose}: {9:Dāma}, {10:Vyāla}, {11:Kaṭa} {12:likewise}.
units.sense: Fashioned by māyā, terrible, like mountains with their wings heaving, those possessors of great māyā arose: Dāma, Vyāla, Kaṭa likewise.

grammar.karakaSummary: nirmitāḥ, bhīmāḥ and pakṣakṣubdhāḥ qualify the nominative plural te; māyayā is the instrumental cause/means of their construction. adryaḥ is the nominative plural standard in the iva comparison. udaguḥ is the finite predicate; Dāma, Vyāla and Kaṭa name its plural subject.
grammar.verbalModality: udaguḥ is a root aorist active 3rd plural of ud-√i, with ga substituted under Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.4.45. nirmitāḥ and kṣubdhāḥ are resultative kta participles.

words.morph: past passive participle, nominative plural masculine
words.note: The pada form restores final -ḥ absent before the following voiced consonant in the saṃhitā line.

words.karaka: karaṇa/hetu, the means or cause of fashioning
words.note: The text names the means as māyā; it does not itself name a machine or mechanism here.
A lexical adjective; no unverified kṛt formation is asserted.
pakṣa can denote a wing or a side/flank; with mountains as the comparison, ‘flanks’ is the contextual line rendering, while both lexical possibilities remain visible here.
Forms the comparison with adrayaḥ.
Saṃhitā ivādrayaḥ = iva + adrayaḥ.

parts.gloss: go; gā is substituted under Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.4.45
aorist with sic elided under Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.4.77
third-plural parasmaipada ending under Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.4.108 and 3.4.110, yielding -uḥ

words.affix: luṅ with sic-lopa (A. 2.4.77); jhi → jus (A. 3.4.108, 3.4.110), prathama-puruṣa bahuvacana parasmaipada
words.note: ud- + √i takes the gā substitute under Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.4.45; in luṅ, sic is elided under 2.4.77 and jhi is replaced by jus under 3.4.108/110, yielding udaguḥ. Kāśikā ad loc. gives agat, agatam, aguḥ.
Resumed by the three following names.

words.gloss: possessors of great māyā; great illusionists
words.note: The masculine agreement makes this ‘those possessing great māyā,’ not the feminine abstract mahāmāyā. Final -ḥ is lost before dāmaḥ in the source saṃhitā.

words.karaka: one member of the compound kartṛ of udaguḥ
words.note: Amarakośa 2.9.74 and Halāyudhakośa line 277 attest dāma/sandāna as a tether for animals; the lexical force is shown without inventing a root derivation.

words.karaka: one member of the compound kartṛ of udaguḥ
words.note: Amarakośa 1.8.7 and 3.3.206 preserve the serpent and beast-of-prey senses; these are parallel lexical values, not competing manufactured etymologies.

words.karaka: one member of the compound kartṛ of udaguḥ
words.note: The local kośa witnesses attest several lexical senses (Halāyudhakośa lines 259, 820; Yādavakośa lines 1909, 2557). The story gives no internal cue that selects a single nirvacana, so the proper name is retained and the ambiguity exposed.
No separate referent is supplied.

units.devanagari: ससर्ज मायया घोरानसुरांस्त्रीन्महाबलान् । बलरक्षार्थमुदितान्कालान्मूर्तिमिव स्थितान्
निर्वृत्ता मायया भीमा बलपादपवाहिनः । उदगुस्ते महामायाः पक्षक्षुब्धा इवाद्रयः
दामो व्यालः कटश्चेति नामभिः परिलाञ्छिताः । यथाप्राप्तैककर्तारश्चेतनामात्रधर्मिणः

units.speaker: Vasiṣṭha
units.devanagari:
वासनात्माभिमानाभ्यां हीनास्ते प्रथमोद्गताः |
नाभिपातं न वापातं न विदुस्ते पलायनम् ||
units.iast:
vāsanātmābhimānābhyāṃ hīnāste prathamodgatāḥ |
nābhipātaṃ na vāpātaṃ na viduste palāyanam ||
units.english: {3:At their first arising}, {2:they} {1:were devoid} {0:of vāsanā and self-identification}; {11:they} {10:knew} {4:neither} {5:attack}, {6,7:nor} {8:falling back}, {9:nor} {12:flight}.
units.sense: At their first arising, they were devoid of vāsanā and self-identification; they knew neither attack, nor falling back, nor flight.

grammar.karakaSummary: vāsanātmābhimānābhyām is an instrumental dual governed by hīnāḥ (‘devoid of’). te is the subject of viduḥ; abhipātam, apātam and palāyanam are its three accusative objects under repeated na. prathamodgatāḥ is a temporal/state predicate of te.
grammar.verbalModality: viduḥ is perfect active 3rd plural used as a stative past (‘they knew’). hīnāḥ and udgatāḥ are kta participles describing their initial condition.

words.karaka: apādāna expressed instrumentally with hīna: that from which they are devoid
words.note: The dual ending is decisive: the two absences are vāsanā and ātma-abhimāna. ‘Self-identification’ renders abhi-√man without replacing it by a metaphysical abstraction.

parallelDerivations.qualification: Directly attested curādi route for the vāsanā member; retained alongside √vās rather than reduced to the compound's primary √man analysis.
Parallel directly attested curādi route, preserving cultivation/habituation within the term's range.

parallelDerivations.analysis: ātmani abhimānaḥ / ātmā iti abhimānaḥ: identification directed to, or taking something as, self
parallelDerivations.qualification: The two vigrahas preserve the objective-locative and iti-predicative readings allowed by the compressed compound.

words.morph: past passive participle, nominative plural masculine
words.karaka: predicate adjective of te; governs the instrumental dual
words.note: Saṃhitā hīnās te = hīnāḥ + te.
Refers to Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa.

words.gloss: at their first arising; newly arisen
words.note: prathama + udgata gives prathamodgata by guṇa sandhi.
First member of the repeated negative series.

words.rootGloss: to go/fall; with abhi-, rush upon
words.note: Saṃhitā nābhipātam = na + abhipātam.
Repeated negative.
Saṃhitā vāpatam = vā + apātam; in the negative series, ‘nor.’
The directional apa- supplies the ‘away/back’ force; ‘retreat’ is the contextual battle sense.
Third negative in the series.

words.karaka: finite predicate; te are kartṛ and three action nouns are karman
words.note: Saṃhitā vidus te = viduḥ + te.
The second te is textually present after viduḥ and must not be collapsed with the earlier pronoun.
The formation is parā + √ay; Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.2.19 upasargasyāyatau and Kāśikā ad loc. directly give plāyate/palāyate through r→l before ay. This is not assigned to an unattested root *palāy.

units.devanagari: अभावात्कर्मणां ते च प्राक्तना नच वासनाः । निर्विकल्पकचिन्मात्रपरिस्पन्दैकधर्मकाः
कर्मजीवकलां तन्वीमसारां च मनोभिदाम् । अपुष्टां कृत्रिमामन्तश्चोदयोदयमागताः
ते ह्यन्धपारम्पर्येण काकतालीयवद्भटाः । प्रकृतामनुवर्तन्ते क्रियामुज्झितवासनाः ।। ३९
अर्धसुप्ता यथा बालाः स्वाङ्गै रिङ्गन्ति केवलम् । वासनात्माभिमानाभ्यां हीनास्ते तद्वदेव हि ।। ४०

units.speaker: Vasiṣṭha
units.devanagari:
न जीवितं न मरणं समरे न जयाजयौ |
केवलं सैनिकानग्रे दृष्ट्वा ते हननोद्यताः ||
units.iast:
na jīvitaṃ na maraṇaṃ samare na jayājayau |
kevalaṃ sainikānagre dṛṣṭvā te hananodyatāḥ ||
units.english: {0:Neither} {1:life} {2:nor} {3:death}, {4:in battle} {5:neither} {6:victory nor defeat}; {7:only}, {10:having seen} {8:the soldiers} {9:before them}, {11:they} {12:were intent on killing}.
units.sense: Neither life nor death, in battle neither victory nor defeat; only, having seen the soldiers before them, they were intent on killing.

grammar.karakaSummary: The first half is an elliptical continuation of na viduḥ: jīvitam, maraṇam and the dual jayājayau are objects, with samare locative. In the second half te are the subject; dṛṣṭvā takes sainikān as object and agre as spatial complement; hananodyatāḥ is the nominal predicate.
grammar.verbalModality: No finite verb is expressed. dṛṣṭvā is a prior-action absolutive; udyatāḥ is a kta predicate expressing their poised/intended state.

words.note: Carries forward the elided viduḥ from 2.46.
The neuter participial noun denotes the state/fact of living.
Repeated negative.
Renders the action noun, not an abstract doctrine of mortality.

words.karaka: adhikaraṇa, the sphere of victory and defeat
words.note: Lexical noun; no speculative derivation is asserted.
The compound itself contains the positive/negative pair.

words.affix: ac in jaya; nañ in ajaya; au (dvitīyā dvivacana)
words.note: jaya + ajaya contracts to jayājaya; a-jaya is literally ‘non-victory,’ contextually defeat.
It limits the trigger to mere seeing.
A secondary derivative meaning one belonging to an army.
Saṃhitā sainikān agre joins across the word boundary.

words.karaka: governs sainikān as karman; shares kartṛ te
words.note: The suppletive participial base dṛṣṭ- is from √dṛś.

words.karaka: kartṛ of dṛṣṭvā and subject of hananodyatāḥ
words.note: Refers to the three artificial warriors.

words.gloss: intent on killing, raised up for killing
words.rootGloss: to restrain/raise/direct; with ud-, be poised
words.affix: lyuṭ in hanana + kta in udyata + jas
words.karaka: predicate adjective of te; hanana is the purpose/complement
words.note: The embedded hanana derives from √han, Dhātupāṭha 02.0002 हनँ हिंसागत्योः (adādi 2P). The head udyata supplies poised/intended action, not autonomous deliberation.

units.speaker: Vasiṣṭha
units.devanagari:
शम्बरश्चिन्तयामास परितुष्टमनास्तदा |
इष्टानिष्टाभिरेते हि वासनाभिर्यदुज्झिताः ||
units.iast:
śambaraścintayāmāsa parituṣṭamanāstadā |
iṣṭāniṣṭābhirete hi vāsanābhiryadujjhitāḥ ||
units.english: {0:Śambara} {1:reflected}, {2:his manas fully satisfied}, {3:then}: ‘{8:Since} {5:these} {6:indeed} {9:are forsaken} {4:by desired and undesired} {7:vāsanās}—
units.sense: Śambara reflected, his manas fully satisfied, then: ‘Since these indeed are forsaken by desired and undesired vāsanās—

grammar.karakaSummary: Śambaraḥ is subject of cintayāmāsa; parituṣṭamanāḥ is his nominative bahuvrīhi predicate and tadā is temporal. The second hemistich preserves the source order iṣṭāniṣṭābhiḥ ete hi vāsanābhiḥ yat ujjhitāḥ: ete is subject of ujjhitāḥ; iṣṭāniṣṭābhiḥ qualifies instrumental plural vāsanābhiḥ, the agency/separation complement of the passive participle; yat introduces the reason continued in 2.49.
grammar.verbalModality: cintayāmāsa is a periphrastic perfect. ujjhitāḥ is a passive/resultative kta form inside Śambara’s thought.

words.note: Saṃhitā śambaraś cintayāmāsa.

parts.gloss: was as the perfect auxiliary, 3rd singular

words.note: The lexical predicate is √cint; āsa is the perfect auxiliary, not a second semantic event.
manas is preserved rather than collapsed into ‘mind’ under the site term policy.
Locates Śambara’s reflection after their construction.

parts.gloss: feminine stem formation agreeing with vāsanā

words.morph: instrumental plural feminine itaretara-dvandva adjective agreeing with vāsanābhiḥ
words.karaka: qualifier within the instrumental complement of ujjhitāḥ
words.note: iṣṭa + aniṣṭa contracts to iṣṭāniṣṭa.
Refers to Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa.
Its explanatory force is preserved.

parts.gloss: dwell; in causative formation, cause to abide/impress

words.rootGloss: to dwell; in causative formation, cause to abide/impress
words.note: The philosophical usage denotes dispositions impressed by attraction and aversion; the line does not reduce vāsanā to memory alone.

parallelDerivations.qualification: Directly attested curādi formation, presented beside the inherited bhvādi dwelling derivation.
Parallel directly attested curādi formation preserving cultivation/habituation.

words.karaka: introduces the reason whose consequence is tad in 2.49
words.note: The verse boundary does not end the syntactic yat–tad construction.

words.morph: past passive participle, nominative plural masculine
words.karaka: predicate of ete; vāsanābhiḥ marks what has left them
words.note: The initial ud-like phonological material belongs to the witnessed root √ujjh itself (Dhātupāṭha 06.0024); no separate ud- prefix is segmented.

units.speaker: Vasiṣṭha
units.devanagari:
तदेते न पलायन्ते देवैरभिहता अपि |
इति निर्णीय दैत्येन्द्रो दामव्यालकटान्विताम् ||
units.iast:
tadete na palāyante devairabhihatā api |
iti nirṇīya daityendro dāmavyālakaṭānvitām ||
units.english: {0:therefore} {1:these} {2:do not} {3:flee}, {6:even} {5:when struck} {4:by the gods}’—{7,8:having determined thus}, {9:the lord of the Daityas}: {10:an army accompanied by Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa}—
units.sense: therefore these do not flee, even when struck by the gods’—having determined thus, the lord of the Daityas: an army accompanied by Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa—

grammar.karakaSummary: tad answers yat in 2.48. ete is subject of na palāyante; abhihatāḥ is concessive with api, and devaiḥ is the passive agent. nirṇīya shares its subject daityendraḥ; dāmavyālakaṭānvitām is accusative feminine agreeing with senām in 2.50.
grammar.verbalModality: palāyante is present middle, generalized as their standing behavior. nirṇīya is an absolutive prior to saṃpreṣayāmāsa in the next verse.

words.note: Saṃhitā tad ete = tadete.
The three warriors.
Direct negation.
parā + √ay with r→l is directly evidenced by Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.2.19 and Kāśikā’s palāyate example.
Instrumental agent with kta.

words.morph: past passive participle, nominative plural masculine
words.karaka: concessive predicate of ete; devaiḥ is agent
words.note: Saṃhitā devair abhihatāḥ.
The force ‘even when’ belongs to api plus the participle.
Marks Śambara’s preceding inference as quoted thought.

words.rootGloss: to lead, bring; with nir-, determine
words.karaka: shares kartṛ daityendraḥ; quoted iti-clause is its content
words.note: The prefix supplies the decisive ‘settle/determine’ sense.
daitya + indra contracts to daityendra.

words.gloss: accompanied by Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa

parts.gloss: feminine stem formation agreeing with senā

words.rootGloss: to go; with anu-, follow/be joined
words.note: The object noun senām is postponed to the next verse; the feminine accusative prevents treating this as a description of Śambara.

units.speaker: Vasiṣṭha
units.devanagari:
सेनां संप्रेषयामास देवेन्द्रबलघातिनीम् |
दैत्याः सागरकुञ्जेभ्यः कन्दरेभ्यश्च सायुधाः ||
units.iast:
senāṃ saṃpreṣayāmāsa devendrabalaghātinīm |
daityāḥ sāgarakuñjebhyaḥ kandarebhyaśca sāyudhāḥ ||
units.english: —{0:that army} {1:he dispatched}, {2:striking Indra’s force}; {3:the Daityas}, {7:armed}, {4:from the ocean-groves} {6:and} {5:from the caverns}—
units.sense: —that army he dispatched, striking Indra’s force; the Daityas, armed, from the ocean-groves and from the caverns—

grammar.karakaSummary: senām is object of saṃpreṣayāmāsa and is qualified by the carried-over dāmavyālakaṭānvitām and by devendrabalaghātinīm. daityāḥ begins the next sentence as subject of udaguḥ in 2.51; the two ablative plurals mark sources and sāyudhāḥ qualifies daityāḥ.
grammar.verbalModality: saṃpreṣayāmāsa is periphrastic perfect 3rd singular. ghātinīm is an agentive adjective (‘striking’), not a finite future.

words.note: Head noun for the two feminine accusative qualifiers spanning 2.49–50.

parts.gloss: was as the perfect auxiliary, 3rd singular

words.rootGloss: to go; causative with pra-, send
words.karaka: finite predicate; daityendraḥ is kartṛ, senām karman
words.note: pra + iṣ yields preṣ- under guṇa; the causative is literally ‘caused to go forth.’

parts.gloss: t-substituted stem before ṇini under Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.3.32
feminine formation after the n-final agent stem, A. 4.1.5

words.affix: √han + ṇini with ghāt substitution under A. 7.3.32; ṅīp (A. 4.1.5) + am (dvitīyā ekavacana)
words.karaka: qualifies senām; devendra-bala is object relation to ghātinī

compound.vigraha: devendrasya balaṃ hanti yā sā, tām ghātinīm

words.note: Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.3.32 prescribes the t/ghāt substitute of √han before the ṇit agent suffix ṇini; Kāśikā gives sādhughātī as the parallel agentive formation.
The syntax continues across the verse boundary.
The spatial word kuñja can be a wooded recess/bower; ‘ocean-recesses’ remains possible.
Second source phrase.
Saṃhitā kandarebhyaś ca.

units.speaker: Vasiṣṭha
units.devanagari:
उदगुर्भीमनिर्ह्रादाः सपक्षगिरिलीलया |
अथोत्तस्थुर्निकुञ्जेभ्यः कन्दरेभ्यः सुरा बलात् ||
units.iast:
udagurbhīmanirhrādāḥ sapakṣagirilīlayā |
athottasthurnikuñjebhyaḥ kandarebhyaḥ surā balāt ||
units.english: —{0:came forth} {1:with terrible roars}, {2:with the play of winged mountains}; {3:then} {7:the gods} {4:rose up} {5:from the bowers} {6:and from the caverns}, {8:forcefully}—
units.sense: —came forth with terrible roars, with the play of winged mountains; then the gods rose up from the bowers and from the caverns, forcefully—

grammar.karakaSummary: The carried-over daityāḥ are subject of udaguḥ; bhīmanirhrādāḥ qualifies them and sapakṣagirilīlayā is an instrumental of manner. surāḥ is subject of uttasthuḥ; the two ablatives mark sources and balāt is adverbial ablative (‘forcefully/in force’).
grammar.verbalModality: udaguḥ is a root aorist active 3rd plural of ud-√i with the Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.4.45 ga substitute; uttasthuḥ is a perfect active 3rd plural of ud-√sthā. The two verbs are not the same tense.

parts.gloss: go; gā is substituted under Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.4.45
aorist with sic elided under Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.4.77
